newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum mill orders weaken in Nov - SpeCTOR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum mill orders weaken in Nov - SpeCTOR.

text.p: Orders in the United States for aluminum mill products fell to 55.4 million pounds per day in November compared to nearly 67 million in September and 63 million in October, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.

"November mill product orders proved to be disappointing," Spector added. Daily orders in November 1995 were 58.3 million. Non-can sheet bookings were unchanged from November 1995. Can sheet bookings, however, after rebounding in September and October, fell sharply in November when they were down nearly 17 percent from year-ago levels.

"The can companies are living off inventories, and just about to enter price negotiations for 1997," Spector said. "After their 1995/1996 pricing experience they are playing their cards close to the vest this year."
Can sheet accounts for about a quarter of global aluminum demand, and can companies have had to swallow a new pricing formula in the past two years.
But Spector said that the National Association of Purchasing Managers' November survey indicated that the U.S. manufacturing sector has historically low inventories.
"With production backlog rising, this suggests that in early 1997 the order pace should pick up," Spector said.
